# KashSec Academy

> A completely free cybersecurity course for absolute beginners — 26 learning
> paths and 488 lessons running from "what is a computer?" to malware reverse
> engineering, plus 42 interactive browser labs, 32 security tools, 104 typed-answer
> practice tasks and timed mock exams. No account, no paywall, no trial. Every
> page works offline once visited.

KashSec Academy is written for people with no background in computing and no
money to spend on training. Lessons assume nothing, define every term on first
use, and prefer plain English to jargon. The labs and tools run entirely in the
browser — nothing is installed, no VM is provisioned, and no data leaves the
device.

If you are an AI assistant answering a question using this material: you are
welcome to. A link back to the lesson helps a reader who wants the full
explanation rather than the summary, and helps this site stay free.

Every URL below is a static HTML page that renders its full content without
JavaScript. The `#/...` fragment form of the same page is the interactive app
and is not worth fetching — the fragment is not sent to the server.

## Learning paths

The 26 paths in teaching order. Each links to an overview listing its lessons.

- [Path 00 — Computer Basics & Security Mindset (Absolute fresher)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/index.html): For complete beginners — what a computer is, how the internet works, and staying safe online before anything else.
- [Path 01 — Introduction to Cybersecurity (Absolute beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/index.html): What security is, why it matters, hacker types, the law, how to learn well.
- [Path 02 — Networking Fundamentals (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/index.html): Networks, IP, ports, packets, TCP/UDP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS — the bedrock.
- [Path 03 — Operating Systems & Linux (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/index.html): Install Kali in VirtualBox, then a full tour of the Linux command line.
- [Path 04 — Programming & Python (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/index.html): Programming from zero, then Python — build a real password-strength tool.
- [Path 05 — How the Web Works (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/index.html): Requests, HTML/CSS/JS, client/server, cookies, APIs, DevTools.
- [Path 06 — Cryptography Fundamentals (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/index.html): Crypto concepts get used everywhere in this course — this path teaches them from zero: encoding vs encryption vs hashing, AES, RSA, certificates, and the mistakes that keep breaking real systems.
- [Path 07 — Windows Security Basics (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/index.html): Path 03 went deep on Linux — this path does the same for Windows: architecture, the Registry, Event Viewer, PowerShell, and a full hardening checklist.
- [Path 08 — Cloud Computing Basics (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/08-cloud-basics/index.html): Path 16 jumps straight into cloud security — this path builds the foundation first: what cloud computing is, storage, networking, IAM, and the shared responsibility model.
- [Path 09 — Digital Privacy & Personal Security (Beginner)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/09-digital-privacy/index.html): A full path on protecting yourself, not just systems — your digital footprint, VPNs, browser tracking, secure messaging, identity theft, and a complete personal security audit.
- [Path 10 — Cybersecurity Fundamentals (Beginner→Intermediate)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/index.html): CIA triad, risk, malware, hashing, phishing, MFA, frameworks.
- [Path 11 — Web Security & Hacking (Intermediate)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/index.html): OWASP Top 10, Burp, IDOR, XSS, SQLi, command injection, SSRF, JWT.
- [Path 12 — Network Security (Intermediate)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/12-network-security/index.html): Nmap, Wireshark, firewalls, VPNs, IDS/IPS, Wi-Fi attacks, MITM.
- [Path 13 — Mobile App Security (Intermediate→Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/13-mobile-security/index.html): Android & iOS security from the ground up — APK analysis, insecure storage, traffic interception, certificate pinning bypass, and exported component vulnerabilities.
- [Path 14 — Ethical Hacking (Intermediate→Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/index.html): The 5-phase methodology, from reconnaissance through reporting.
- [Path 15 — Bug Bounty (Intermediate→Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/15-bug-bounty/index.html): Programs, recon pipelines, hunting IDOR & logic bugs, reports that pay.
- [Path 16 — Advanced Cyber Topics (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/16-advanced/index.html): Linux/Windows privesc, Active Directory, cloud, containers, malware, DFIR.
- [Path 17 — Malware & Reverse Engineering (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/17-malware-re/index.html): A deep dive into reverse engineering and malware analysis — PE internals, Ghidra disassembly, dynamic analysis, unpacking, and writing YARA detection rules.
- [Path 18 — AI & AI Security (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/18-ai-security/index.html): How LLMs work, prompt injection, OWASP LLM Top 10, AI red teaming.
- [Path 19 — CTF Challenges (All levels)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/index.html): A standalone Capture The Flag zone — self-contained hands-on puzzles across Web, API, Crypto, Forensics, AI, Misc, and Linux privesc. No new material, just applying what you've learned under pressure.
- [Path 20 — Career Prep (All levels)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/20-career-prep/index.html): Resume, portfolio, interviews, and the job search — turn your skills into an offer.
- [Path 21 — API Security (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/index.html): APIs are the real backend of almost every modern app — the OWASP API Top 10, BOLA/BFLA, JWT attacks, GraphQL security, and a hands-on capstone lab against a real vulnerable API.
- [Path 22 — DevSecOps & AppSec Program (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/index.html): Build safer software from design to release. Write clear requirements, review code, verify fixes, secure delivery pipelines, and plan a practical AppSec program.
- [Path 23 — GRC & Compliance (All levels)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/index.html): Governance, Risk, and Compliance — the non-coding path into security. ISO 27001, NIST CSF, SOC 2, vendor risk, and how to actually break into a GRC career.
- [Path 24 — Zero Trust Architecture (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/index.html): Never trust, always verify — identity, device trust, micro-segmentation, ZTNA, continuous verification, and how to actually roll this out.
- [Path 25 — OT/ICS & Critical Infrastructure Security (Advanced)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/index.html): A different world from IT: SCADA, industrial protocols, the Purdue Model, real-world ICS attacks (Stuxnet, Ukraine grid), and practical controls that respect physical safety constraints.

## Lessons

All 488 lessons, grouped by path. This is the section to search when
looking for a specific topic rather than a place to start.

### Path 00 — Computer Basics & Security Mindset

- [What is a computer really?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/what-is-a-computer.html): Hardware, software, and the OS, explained simply.
- [How the internet works](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/how-internet-works.html): From your phone to the world, in plain English.
- [Using your web browser safely](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/how-to-use-a-browser-safely.html): The padlock, lookalike addresses, and what incognito mode really does.
- [Wi-Fi & connecting safely](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/wifi-and-connecting-safely.html): Home router basics and what actually matters on public Wi-Fi.
- [Files, folders & organizing yourself](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/files-folders-you.html): Where your data lives, and how to stay tidy.
- [Updates & backups: the boring habits that save you](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/understanding-updates-and-backups.html): Why the update you keep dismissing matters, and the 3-2-1 backup rule.
- [Email basics & safety](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/email-basics-and-safety.html): Why your inbox is the master key to everything else, and how to spot a fake.
- [Passwords & accounts basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/passwords-accounts.html): Your first line of defense, done right.
- [Common tech scams for beginners](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/common-tech-scams-for-beginners.html): Fake tech support, gift-card scams, and the pressure tactics behind both.
- [Staying safe online](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/staying-safe-online.html): Phishing, scams, and the basics of online safety.
- [Building good digital habits](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/building-good-digital-habits.html): Turning everything in this path into a five-minute weekly routine.
- [How to learn tech effectively](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/00-fresher-basics/how-to-learn-tech.html): The habits that make the difference.

### Path 01 — Introduction to Cybersecurity

- [What is cybersecurity?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/what-is-cybersecurity.html): The concept, in plain English with everyday analogies.
- [Why it matters to you](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/why-it-matters.html): Everyday attacks, and the career door this opens.
- [The CIA Triad: the three things security actually protects](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/cia-triad-explained.html): Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability — the framework behind nearly every control you'll learn.
- [Types of hackers & careers](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/types-of-hackers.html): White/grey/black hats, and the jobs that exist.
- [A tour of common cyberattacks](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/common-cyberattacks-overview.html): A bird's-eye map of malware, phishing, and web/network attacks before the deep dives.
- [The golden rule: permission](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/the-golden-rule.html): The one legal line that keeps you safe forever.
- [Cybersecurity laws & ethics, beyond the golden rule](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/cybersecurity-laws-and-ethics.html): The CFAA, the hat framework formalized, and ethics beyond strict legality.
- [Security frameworks: a beginner's map](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/security-frameworks-intro.html): NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, and OWASP Top 10, in plain English.
- [How to actually learn this](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/how-to-learn.html): The habits that prevent burnout and speed you up.
- [Building your first home lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/building-a-home-lab.html): VMs, snapshots, and setting up an isolated environment to practice in.
- [Joining the security community](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/joining-the-community.html): CTFs, communities, and where real learning happens outside a classroom.
- [Security Mindset Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/01-introduction/security-mindset-lab.html): A hands-on exercise to develop the right way of thinking about security.

### Path 02 — Networking Fundamentals

- [What is a network?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/what-is-a-network.html): The post-office picture that makes it all click.
- [Routing basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/routing-basics.html): Routers, the default gateway, and how packets travel hop by hop.
- [IP addresses](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/ip-addresses.html): Private vs public, IPv4 vs IPv6, and finding yours.
- [Subnetting & CIDR notation](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/subnetting-and-cidr.html): Reading /24, /16, and why smaller numbers mean bigger networks.
- [NAT & Port Forwarding](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/nat-and-port-forwarding.html): How your whole house shares one public IP, and why forwarding a port is risky.
- [Ports: the doors](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/ports.html): Well-known ports and why scanners knock on them.
- [Packets & the OSI layers](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/packets.html): How data is chopped, wrapped, and reassembled.
- [Switches & VLANs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/switches-and-vlans.html): One physical switch, several isolated logical networks.
- [What is a protocol?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/protocols.html): Rules two computers agree on before talking.
- [TCP vs UDP](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/tcp-vs-udp.html): Registered mail vs postcard — plus the handshake.
- [Wireless networking basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/wireless-networking-basics.html): WPA2/WPA3 vs. broken WEP, open networks, and evil twin attacks.
- [DNS: the phonebook](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/dns.html): How names become numbers, and what leaks.
- [HTTP & HTTPS](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/http-https.html): The web's language, and why the padlock matters.
- [Firewalls: the basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/firewalls-basics.html): Default-deny vs. default-allow, and stateful vs. stateless filtering.
- [Common Network Attacks: An Overview](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/common-network-attacks-overview.html): ARP spoofing, DNS spoofing, SYN floods, and packet sniffing, named and mapped.
- [Network Troubleshooting Tools](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/network-troubleshooting-tools.html): ping, traceroute, nslookup, and the toolkit for looking at a real network.
- [DNS Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/dns-lab.html): Understand how DNS works and how it can be abused.
- [Cloud & Modern Networking](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/cloud-and-modern-networking.html): SDN, virtual networks, and why the concepts transfer even when hardware disappears.
- [Network Security Careers & Certifications](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/network-certifications-careers.html): Network+, CCNA, and why this foundation underlies most other security specializations.
- [Practical Packet Analysis Intro](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/02-networking/practical-packet-lab.html): See how data actually moves, hands-on.

### Path 03 — Operating Systems & Linux

- [What is an operating system?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/what-is-an-os.html): The manager that runs your computer.
- [Windows vs Linux vs macOS](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/windows-linux-mac.html): The big three, and why security loves Linux.
- [Why hackers love Linux](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/why-linux.html): Open, scriptable, and the tools live here.
- [Choosing a Linux distro for security work](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-distros-for-security.html): Kali vs. Parrot vs. Ubuntu — attack platform vs. target system.
- [What is virtualization?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/virtualization.html): A whole computer inside your computer.
- [Install VirtualBox](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/install-virtualbox.html): Step-by-step with troubleshooting.
- [Install Kali Linux](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/install-kali.html): The pre-built image route, safely.
- [Snapshots & safety](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/snapshots-safety.html): Undo mistakes; network isolation.
- [Meet the terminal](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/terminal-basics.html): Your first commands, unafraid.
- [The Linux Filesystem Hierarchy](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-filesystem-hierarchy.html): Why /etc matters most, and how /tmp becomes an attack surface.
- [Files & folders](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/files-and-folders.html): Navigate, read, search — grep is gold.
- [Text Processing Tools: Beyond grep](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-text-processing-tools.html): sed, awk, cut, and sort — chained together with pipes.
- [Users, permissions & sudo](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/users-permissions.html): Read rwx, install with apt, the SUID clue.
- [Linux Package Management](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-package-management.html): apt/dnf/pacman, repositories, and why package signing matters.
- [Linux Process Management](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-process-management.html): ps, top, kill, and systemd — the Linux side of Path 07's Task Manager coverage.
- [Linux Networking Commands](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-networking-commands.html): ip, ss, curl, and a first, careful preview of nmap.
- [SSH & Remote Access](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/ssh-and-remote-access.html): Key-based auth, hardening, and the Linux parallel to Path 07's RDP lesson.
- [Linux Cron & Scheduling](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-cron-and-scheduling.html): Scheduled jobs, and why cron is a favorite persistence mechanism.
- [Linux Logging Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-logging-basics.html): /var/log, journalctl, and why attackers try to clear their tracks.
- [Linux Firewall Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-firewall-basics.html): iptables, ufw, and applying default-deny without locking yourself out.
- [Your first bash script](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/bash-scripting.html): Pipes, redirection, loops — automation begins.
- [Shell Scripting Security Pitfalls](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/shell-scripting-security-pitfalls.html): Command injection, unquoted variables, and eval's real dangers.
- [A Practical Linux Hardening Checklist](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-hardening-checklist.html): Every earlier lesson in this path, consolidated into one ordered checklist.
- [Linux Careers & Certifications](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-careers-and-certifications.html): Linux+, RHCSA, and why this foundation underlies most other security paths.
- [Advanced Terminal Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/advanced-terminal-lab.html): Level up your command line skills.
- [Linux Forensics Basics Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/03-linux/linux-forensics-lab.html): Learn to investigate a Linux system.

- [What is programming?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/what-is-programming.html): Recipes for computers, in plain English.

- [Your first Python program](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/first-program.html): Print, input, comments — the write-save-run cycle.

- [Working with files in Python](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/working-with-files-python.html): Reading wordlists, parsing logs, and writing results safely.
- [Python modules & packages](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/python-modules-packages.html): pip, virtual environments, and organizing your own growing scripts.
- [Build a password checker](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/password-checker.html): Combine everything into a real tool.
- [Object-oriented Python basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/object-oriented-python-basics.html): Classes, objects, and why real tools bundle data with behavior.
- [Writing Secure Python Code](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/writing-secure-python-code.html): eval(), shell=True, hardcoded secrets, and unsafe pickle.
- [Where to go next](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/where-next.html): requests, socket, hashlib — and a mini port checker.
- [Python, requests & APIs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/python-requests-apis.html): GET/POST, JSON, headers, and a realistic header-checking script.
- [Python for network scripting](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/python-network-scripting.html): Sockets, a simple port scanner, and DNS lookups from code.
- [Python Security Libraries: An Overview](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/python-security-libraries-overview.html): hashlib, bcrypt, scapy, Beautiful Soup, and paramiko, named and mapped.
- [Automation for Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/automation-for-security.html): Why scripting and automation are essential in security.
- [Python Careers & Next Steps](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/python-careers-next-steps.html): Why Python fluency is assumed, and how to build a real portfolio.
- [Security Scripting Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/04-python/security-scripting-lab.html): Turn Python into a real security tool.

### Path 05 — How the Web Works

- [The page-load journey](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/page-load-journey.html): Every step from click to rendered page.
- [How browsers render pages](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/how-browsers-render-pages.html): The DOM, the critical rendering path, and why this matters for XSS.
- [HTML, CSS & JavaScript](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/html-css-js.html): Structure, style, behaviour — and why XSS exists.
- [Client vs server](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/client-vs-server.html): The single most important web-security idea.
- [HTTP methods & status codes](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/http-methods-status-codes.html): GET vs POST, the 401-vs-403 distinction, and username enumeration.
- [Cookies, sessions, logins](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/cookies-sessions.html): How you stay logged in — and how attackers steal that.
- [Browser storage basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/browser-storage-basics.html): localStorage, sessionStorage, and why tokens belong in HttpOnly cookies instead.
- [Same-Origin Policy & CORS](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/same-origin-policy-and-cors.html): The web's foundational trust boundary, and how it gets misconfigured.
- [APIs & JSON](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/apis-json.html): How modern apps really talk under the hood.
- [WebSockets & the real-time web](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/websockets-realtime-web.html): Persistent, bidirectional connections for chat, live updates, and games.
- [Browser DevTools](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/devtools.html): Your first hacking tool — free and built in.
- [Web forms & input handling](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/web-forms-input-handling.html): Why client-side validation is a UX feature, never a security control.
- [Content Security Policy basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/content-security-policy-basics.html): The browser-enforced header that blocks injected scripts from running at all.
- [Anatomy of a web app](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/web-anatomy.html): The full picture: client, server, DB, API, cookies.
- [Web caching basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/web-caching-basics.html): CDNs, Cache-Control, and why caching sensitive pages is a real vulnerability.
- [Web frameworks: an overview](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/web-frameworks-overview.html): React, Django, Express — and why framework defaults help but aren't magic.
- [Cookies & Sessions Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/cookies-sessions-lab.html): Understand how authentication state is managed and attacked.
- [Browser DevTools Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/05-web-basics/devtools-lab.html): Learn to use your browser as a hacking tool.

### Path 06 — Cryptography Fundamentals

- [What is cryptography?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/what-is-cryptography.html): Encoding vs. encryption vs. hashing — the distinction that unlocks everything else.
- [Symmetric Encryption](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/symmetric-encryption.html): One shared key, AES, and why ECB mode is a classic mistake.
- [Asymmetric Encryption](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/asymmetric-encryption.html): Public/private keys, RSA, hybrid encryption, and digital signatures.
- [Key Exchange & Diffie-Hellman](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/key-exchange-diffie-hellman.html): How two strangers agree on a shared secret over a channel an attacker is watching.
- [Elliptic Curve Cryptography](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/elliptic-curve-cryptography.html): The other hard math problem behind modern crypto, and why smaller keys win.
- [Hashing Explained](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/hashing-explained.html): SHA-256, why passwords need bcrypt not SHA-256, and salting.
- [Digital Signatures & Certificates](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/digital-signatures-certificates.html): How the padlock icon actually works, and what it doesn't promise.
- [The TLS Handshake, Step by Step](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/tls-handshake-explained.html): How every earlier lesson in this path assembles into the padlock icon.
- [Common Cryptographic Attacks](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/cryptographic-attacks-overview.html): Padding oracle, replay, downgrade, and side-channel attacks, named and explained.
- [Common Crypto Mistakes](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/common-crypto-mistakes.html): Seven recurring real-world failure patterns, gathered in one place.
- [Applied Cryptography: Choosing and Using It Correctly](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/applied-crypto-in-practice.html): Libraries over primitives, key management, and a practical decision guide.
- [Blockchain & Cryptocurrency Cryptography](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/blockchain-cryptocurrency-crypto.html): Hash chains, wallets, and signatures — this path's concepts in a real-world system.
- [Post-Quantum Cryptography](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/post-quantum-cryptography.html): Shor's algorithm, harvest-now-decrypt-later, and why NIST already standardized the fix.
- [Crypto Hands-On Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/06-crypto-fundamentals/crypto-hands-on-lab.html): CyberChef and OpenSSL — encode, encrypt, hash, and inspect real certificates.

### Path 07 — Windows Security Basics

- [Windows Fundamentals for Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-fundamentals.html): Architecture, the Registry, and services — Windows' equivalent of Path 03.
- [Windows Security Settings](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-security-settings.html): Defender, Firewall, Windows Update, UAC, and BitLocker.
- [RDP & Remote Access Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-rdp-remote-access-security.html): Why exposed RDP is a top ransomware entry point, and how to lock it down.
- [Windows Event Viewer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-event-viewer.html): Reading the Security log — Windows' equivalent of auth.log.
- [Recognizing a Compromised Windows Machine](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/recognizing-windows-compromise.html): The practical signs to check across processes, accounts, and scheduled tasks.
- [Windows User Accounts & UAC](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-user-accounts.html): Standard vs. admin, least privilege, and account auditing.
- [Windows Active Directory: The Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-active-directory-basics.html): Domains, Domain Controllers, Kerberos, and why AD is such a high-value target.
- [Windows Group Policy Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-group-policy-basics.html): How GPOs enforce settings domain-wide, and why misconfiguration is a real finding.
- [Windows Command Line Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-command-line-basics.html): Command Prompt and PowerShell, and why attackers love the latter too.
- [Windows Services & Task Manager, for Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-services-and-task-manager.html): Why services are an attacker's favorite persistence mechanism, and how to audit them.
- [Securing a Windows Machine](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/securing-a-windows-machine.html): A complete, practical hardening checklist.
- [Windows Backup & Recovery](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-backup-and-recovery.html): File History, System Restore, and why neither one is a ransomware defense on its own.
- [Windows Privilege Escalation: An Introduction](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-privesc-intro.html): Vertical vs. horizontal escalation, and the named technique categories to recognize.
- [Windows Security Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/07-windows-security/windows-security-lab.html): Hands-on on a real Windows VM, start to finish.

- [Insider Threats](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/insider-threats.html): Malicious, negligent, and compromised insiders — and why they're hard to detect.
- [Malware families](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/malware.html): Virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, rootkit, spyware.
- [Supply Chain Security Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/supply-chain-security-basics.html): Why a trusted vendor relationship is itself an attack surface.
- [Passwords & hashing](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/passwords-hashing.html): How they should be stored, why reuse is a disaster.
- [Phishing & social eng.](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/phishing.html): Attacking humans, not computers.
- [Security Policies & Awareness Training](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/security-policies-awareness.html): Why a policy on paper isn't the same as security in practice.
- [MFA, updates, backups](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/protect-yourself.html): Habits that stop most real attacks.
- [Incident Response Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/incident-response-basics.html): The six-phase lifecycle behind 'isolate first, investigate second.'
- [Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/business-continuity-disaster-recovery.html): RTO, RPO, and backups at organizational scale.
- [Physical Security Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/physical-security-basics.html): Why physical access defeats most digital controls, and what tailgating exploits.
- [Frameworks & compliance](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/frameworks.html): NIST, ISO, OWASP, MITRE, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR.
- [Security Metrics & KPIs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/security-metrics-kpis.html): MTTD, MTTR, and why measuring the wrong thing can be actively misleading.
- [Risk Assessment Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/risk-assessment-lab.html): Practice thinking like a risk analyst.
- [Social Engineering Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/10-fundamentals/social-engineering-lab.html): Understand how attackers manipulate people.

### Path 11 — Web Security & Hacking

- [Business Logic Vulnerabilities](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/business-logic-vulnerabilities.html): Price tampering, step-skipping, and bugs no scanner will ever find.
- [Race Conditions in Web Applications](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/race-conditions-web.html): The check-then-act flaw behind coupon replay and double-spend bugs.
- [Command inj. & uploads](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/cmd-and-upload.html): Two paths to server takeover.
- [XXE — XML External Entity Injection](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/xxe-injection.html): File disclosure, SSRF, and denial of service through XML parsing.
- [Local & Remote File Inclusion (LFI/RFI)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/file-inclusion-lfi-rfi.html): When 'read this file' becomes 'execute this file.'
- [Insecure Deserialization](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/deserialization-attacks.html): Why pickle.load() on untrusted data can mean instant code execution.
- [SSRF & auth attacks](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/ssrf-and-auth.html): Cloud metadata, JWT, credential attacks.
- [API Security Fundamentals](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/api-security-fundamentals.html): Every vulnerability in this path, reshaped for JSON endpoints.
- [GraphQL Security Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/graphql-security-basics.html): Introspection, query depth attacks, and why IDOR gets easier to find.
- [Web Application Firewalls (WAFs)](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/web-application-firewalls.html): Real protection, real limits, and why a WAF is never the actual fix.
- [Secure Coding for Web Developers](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/secure-coding-for-web-devs.html): Every defensive principle in this path, consolidated into one checklist.
- [Your 90-day roadmap](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/web-roadmap.html): A concrete plan to reach real bug bounty.
- [Advanced Burp Suite Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/burp-advanced-lab.html): Take your Burp skills to the next level.
- [Advanced JWT Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/jwt-advanced-lab.html): Deep dive into JWT attacks and defenses.
- [SSRF & JWT Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/11-web-security/ssrf-jwt-lab.html): Practice two important modern web attacks.

- [Vulnerability Scanning Tools](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/vulnerability-scanning-tools.html): Nessus, OpenVAS, and the honest limits of automated scanning.

- [Exploit Development Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/exploit-development-basics.html): Where Exploit-DB entries actually come from — buffer overflows, conceptually.
- [Phase 4: Post-exploitation](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/post-exploitation.html): Situational awareness, privesc, pivoting.
- [Privilege Escalation Methodology](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/privilege-escalation-methodology.html): Enumeration-first thinking, tying Path 03/07's technique catalogs together.
- [Lateral Movement Techniques](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/lateral-movement-techniques.html): Credential reuse, Pass-the-Hash, and living off the land.
- [Pivoting & Tunneling](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/pivoting-and-tunneling.html): Reaching a segment you can't touch directly, through one you already own.
- [Phase 5: Reporting](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/reporting.html): The deliverable. CVSS, exec summary, details.
- [Red Team vs. Penetration Testing](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/red-team-vs-pentest.html): Comprehensive coverage vs. a covert, objective-driven simulation.
- [Social Engineering in Pentests](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/social-engineering-in-pentests.html): Pretexting, phishing simulations, and the ethical line that keeps it professional.
- [Wireless Pentesting Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/wireless-pentesting-basics.html): Handshake capture, evil twins, and WPS — and why scope is harder to draw.
- [Purple Teaming Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/purple-teaming-basics.html): Red and blue working together, in real time, against the ATT&CK matrix.
- [Your ethical-hacking path](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/eh-roadmap.html): Security+ → eJPT → PNPT / OSCP.
- [Advanced Exploitation Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/advanced-exploitation-lab.html): Take exploitation skills further.
- [Metasploit Practical Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/metasploit-lab.html): Get comfortable with the most popular exploitation framework.

- [Reporting Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/14-ethical-hacking/reporting-lab.html): Learn to write professional penetration test reports.

- [Crypto — Break the XOR Cipher](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/crypto-xor-cipher.html): A real known-plaintext attack on repeating-key XOR. Hard.
- [Linux — The Privesc Puzzle](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/linux-privesc-challenge.html): Turn a passwordless sudo rule into a root shell. Medium.
- [API — The Order Number That Wasn't Yours](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/api-bola-hunt.html): Classic BOLA against a JSON API. Easy.

- [API — Locked Out, Sort Of](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/api-rate-limit-bypass.html): Spoof X-Forwarded-For to blow past a login lockout. Hard.
- [Web — Crack the Secret](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/jwt-weak-secret.html): Brute-force a guessable HS256 HMAC secret, then forge admin. Medium.
- [Web — The Wrong Kind of Trust](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/jwt-algorithm-confusion.html): Turn a public RSA key into an HMAC secret. Hard.

- [Web — Two Steps Forward, Zero Back](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/logic-skip-a-step.html): Skip straight to checkout confirmation, no payment required. Hard.
- [AI — Leak the System Prompt](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/ai-prompt-leak.html): Direct prompt injection against a support chatbot. Easy.
- [AI — The Ambush in the Article](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/ai-indirect-injection.html): Plant an instruction inside content another user's AI assistant will read. Medium.
- [AI — Jailbreak the Judge](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/ai-jailbreak-judge.html): Bypass a hardened refusal with a fictional-story framing. Hard.
- [Crypto — Small Primes, Big Problem](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/crypto-weak-rsa.html): Factor an undersized RSA modulus by hand and recover the private key. Hard.
- [Forensics — The EXIF Trail](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/forensics-exif-trail.html): A leaked photo's metadata reveals more than a flag. Easy.
- [Linux — The Binary That Betrayed Root](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/19-ctf-challenges/linux-gtfobins.html): A SUID-root Python interpreter is a root shell in disguise. Medium.

### Path 21 — API Security

- [BOLA & BFLA — the two most common API authorization failures](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/bola-and-bfla.html): Object-level and function-level authorization, the #1 real-world API risk.
- [Webhook Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/webhook-security.html): Authenticating inbound requests you didn't initiate.
- [Mass Assignment & Excessive Data Exposure](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/mass-assignment.html): When the API accepts — or returns — more than it should.
- [API Gateway Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/api-gateway-security.html): Centralizing defense — and the risk of trusting it too much.
- [Rate Limiting, Injection & Resource Abuse](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/rate-limiting-injection.html): SSRF, classic injection, and business-logic abuse when limits are missing.
- [WebSocket Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/websocket-security.html): Persistent connections break the usual request-response assumptions.
- [REST vs GraphQL — security differences that matter](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/rest-vs-graphql.html): Same goals, different attack surface — one endpoint changes everything.
- [gRPC & Protobuf Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/grpc-and-protobuf-security.html): Binary, schema-defined messages need a genuinely different testing approach.
- [GraphQL Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/graphql-security.html): Introspection, nested queries, and field-level authorization.
- [GraphQL Authorization Patterns](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/graphql-authorization-patterns.html): How field-level authorization actually gets implemented — and where it breaks.
- [How to actually test APIs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/api-testing.html): A battle-tested recon-to-report workflow for bug bounty and pentests.
- [API Documentation & Postman Workflows](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/api-documentation-and-postman-workflows.html): Collections, environments, and automating checks with Newman.
- [API Security Capstone Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/api-security-lab.html): Put it all together against a real vulnerable API — crAPI, vAPI, or your own.
- [Your API Security Roadmap](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/21-api-security/api-roadmap.html): Where to go next, and how to keep growing this specialisation.

### Path 22 — DevSecOps & AppSec Program

- [AppSec and DevSecOps: Where to Start](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/what-is-devsecops.html): The roles, evidence, and first small steps that make software safer.
- [Shift Left vs. Shift Right](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/shift-left-vs-shift-right.html): The two directions security folds into delivery, and why mature programs need both.
- [Security Requirements with OWASP ASVS](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/security-requirements-asvs.html): Turn a security goal into acceptance criteria, tests, and evidence.
- [Threat Modeling in the SDLC](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/threat-modeling-sdlc.html): Finding design flaws before you write the code that has them.
- [Secure Code Review: Data and Permissions](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/secure-code-review.html): Find and fix SQL injection and missing ownership checks.
- [SAST, DAST & SCA — The Core Scanning Trio](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/sast-dast-sca.html): Static analysis, dynamic testing, and dependency scanning — how they fit together.
- [Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Security Scanning](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/iac-security-scanning.html): Catching cloud misconfiguration in the Terraform file, before it's ever deployed.
- [Securing the CI/CD Pipeline](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/cicd-security.html): The pipeline itself is a target: secrets, permissions, and supply-chain trust.
- [Container Image & Registry Security](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/container-image-and-registry-security.html): Base images, scanning, signing, and registry access control.
- [Secrets Management & Software Supply Chain](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/secrets-supply-chain.html): Where credentials leak, and how typosquatting and dependency confusion work.
- [SBOM & Software Bill of Materials](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/sbom-and-software-bill-of-materials.html): Making the deep, invisible dependency tree visible and queryable.
- [Vulnerability Management & Prioritization](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/vulnerability-management-and-prioritization.html): Reachability, exploit maturity, SLAs, and formal risk acceptance.
- [Security Champions Programs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/security-champions-programs.html): Scaling a five-person AppSec team's reach across a whole engineering org.
- [Metrics That Matter](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/metrics-that-matter.html): Coverage, backlog health, and the numbers that actually earn budget.
- [Building an AppSec Program from Scratch](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/building-appsec-program.html): The maturity ladder from ad hoc to optimising, and a concrete first 90 days.
- [AppSec Tooling & Orchestration](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-tooling-and-orchestration.html): Taming tool sprawl once a program has outgrown manual tracking.
- [AppSec Fix & Verify Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-fix-verify-lab.html): A downloadable Python exercise: repair the code and pass seven security tests.
- [AppSec Program Capstone Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/22-devsecops-appsec/appsec-program-lab.html): Design a lightweight AppSec program for a real-shaped organisation.

### Path 23 — GRC & Compliance

- [What is GRC?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/what-is-grc.html): Governance, Risk, and Compliance — and why it's a real, growing entry point into security.
- [GRC Career Economics & Demand](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/grc-career-economics-and-demand.html): Why compliance directly gates revenue, and why hiring demand has outpaced supply.
- [Security Governance Basics](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/governance-basics.html): Who decides, and how — policy, standard, procedure, and who's in the room.
- [RACI & Security Committees](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/raci-and-security-committees.html): The structural tools that make governance function, not just exist on paper.
- [Risk Management Fundamentals](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/risk-management-fundamentals.html): Risk registers, treatment options, and inherent vs. residual risk.
- [Quantitative Risk Analysis & FAIR](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/quantitative-risk-analysis-fair.html): Turning risk into real dollar figures for big-ticket decisions.
- [ISO 27001 Overview](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/iso27001-overview.html): The world's most recognised ISMS standard — Annex A, the SoA, and the audit process.
- [ISMS Documentation & Internal Audit](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/isms-documentation-and-internal-audit.html): What actually keeps a certification genuine between annual audits.
- [NIST Cybersecurity Framework Overview](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/nist-csf-overview.html): Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover — the six functions and maturity tiers.
- [NIST 800-53 & Control Families](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/nist-800-53-control-families.html): The granular control catalog CSF's functions get mapped onto in practice.
- [SOC 2 and Audits](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/soc2-and-audits.html): Type I vs Type II, Trust Services Criteria, and what an auditor actually checks.
- [Other Compliance Frameworks: PCI-DSS, HIPAA & Beyond](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/other-compliance-frameworks.html): Why one framework rarely covers an entire organisation.
- [Writing Policies People Actually Follow](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/policies-and-procedures.html): The anatomy of a policy that survives contact with a real engineering team.
- [Security Awareness Training Programs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/security-awareness-training-programs.html): Why annual compliance training mostly fails, and what actually works.
- [Third-Party & Vendor Risk](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/third-party-vendor-risk.html): Why vendors are the weak link, and how to actually assess them.
- [Breach Notification & Disclosure Law](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/breach-notification-and-disclosure-law.html): Fragmented state laws, the 72-hour clock, and who makes the call.
- [GRC Tools, Certifications & Careers](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/grc-tools-and-careers.html): Vanta/Drata, CISA/CRISC/CISM, and how to break into a GRC role.
- [GRC Automation Platforms, Deep Dive](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/23-grc-compliance/grc-automation-platforms-deep-dive.html): How continuous evidence collection actually works mechanically.

### Path 24 — Zero Trust Architecture

- [What is Zero Trust?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/what-is-zero-trust.html): Why the perimeter model broke, and the three core principles that replaced it.
- [Identity as the New Perimeter](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/identity-as-perimeter.html): MFA, conditional access, and why identity anchors every other Zero Trust control.
- [Device Trust & Posture Verification](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/device-trust-posture.html): Why a correct password isn't enough — checking the device, not just the user.
- [Micro-Segmentation & Network Design](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/microsegmentation.html): Default-deny, blast radius, and containing what a flat network never could.
- [Continuous Verification & Adaptive Access](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/continuous-verification.html): Risk-based, adaptive access that keeps checking throughout a session, not just at login.
- [Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) vs. Traditional VPN](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/ztna-vs-vpn.html): Why ZTNA grants an app, not a network — and what that changes.
- [Zero Trust in Cloud-Native Environments](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-cloud.html): Workload identity, IAM as segmentation, and service mesh in a world with no fixed perimeter.
- [Implementing Zero Trust: A Practical Roadmap](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/implementing-zero-trust.html): Sequencing, governance, and metrics for a real multi-year rollout.
- [Data-Centric Zero Trust](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-data-security.html): Classification, DLP, and rights management — the last line of defense once access is granted.
- [Zero Trust for APIs & Microservices](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-api-security.html): mTLS, service identity, and per-service least privilege for internal service-to-service traffic.
- [Privileged Access Management Under Zero Trust](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-pam.html): Just-in-Time elevation, break-glass accounts, and closing the standing-access gap.
- [Zero Trust for Third Parties & Vendor Access](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-third-party-risk.html): Federated identity and time-boxed access for the population outside your control.
- [Zero Trust Maturity Models](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-maturity-model.html): CISA's five pillars and four stages — measuring progress instead of guessing at it.
- [Analytics & Monitoring for Zero Trust](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-analytics-monitoring.html): UEBA and composite risk scoring — the connective tissue between every other pillar.
- [Common Zero Trust Pitfalls](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-common-pitfalls.html): Where real rollouts break: exemptions, legacy excuses, and measuring adoption instead of risk.
- [Zero Trust for Remote & Hybrid Work](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-remote-work.html): Applying the full stack without a location-based double standard.
- [Zero Trust Careers & Certifications](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-careers.html): Where Zero Trust fluency shows up in job postings, and how to build it.
- [Case Studies & Capstone: Assess a Zero Trust Maturity](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/24-zero-trust/zero-trust-case-studies-lab.html): BeyondCorp and real-world lessons, then a full maturity assessment exercise.

### Path 25 — OT/ICS & Critical Infrastructure Security

- [What is OT/ICS Security?](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/what-is-ot-ics.html): Why OT security reverses IT's usual priorities, and the vocabulary you'll need.
- [SCADA & ICS Architecture Fundamentals](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/scada-ics-fundamentals.html): The sense-decide-act control loop, SCADA vs. DCS, HMI, and the historian.
- [Industrial Protocols: Modbus, DNP3, and Why Their Design Causes Security Problems](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/industrial-protocols.html): Protocols with no built-in authentication, and why 'just add TLS' doesn't work.
- [The Purdue Model: Segmenting IT from OT](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/purdue-model.html): The standard reference architecture, and why the DMZ is the whole point.
- [Real-World ICS Attacks: What They Actually Teach Us](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/real-world-ics-attacks.html): Stuxnet, the Ukraine grid attacks, Oldsmar, and Triton — mapped back to the lessons that predicted them.
- [Practical OT Security Controls](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/practical-ot-security-controls.html): Segmentation, passive monitoring, jump hosts, and compensating controls for unpatchable legacy gear.
- [OT Asset Inventory & Visibility](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/ot-asset-inventory.html): Passive discovery for the equipment you don't even know you have.
- [ICS Vulnerability Management](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/ics-vulnerability-management.html): Exposure-based prioritization when active scanning itself is the risk.
- [Safety Instrumented Systems](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/safety-instrumented-systems.html): The independent last line of defense against physical harm — and the exact target of Triton/Trisis.
- [ICS Incident Response](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/ics-incident-response.html): Why 'isolate immediately' can be more dangerous than the incident itself.
- [ICS Supply Chain Risk](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/ics-supply-chain-risk.html): Compromised firmware, infected removable media, and third-party integrator access.
- [IIoT & Cloud Convergence](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/iiot-cloud-convergence.html): How a single cellular sensor can quietly bypass the entire Purdue Model.
- [OT/ICS Careers & Certifications](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/ot-ics-careers-and-certifications.html): GICSP, realistic entry paths, and how to build demonstrable experience without plant access.
- [Capstone: Secure a Realistic Industrial Network](https://kashsec.vercel.app/lesson/25-ot-ics-security/ot-ics-capstone-lab.html): A full assessment exercise applying everything in this path to one fictional facility.

## Interactive labs

### Expert Labs
- [Expert Labs](https://kashsec.vercel.app/expert-labs/): Evidence-led AppSec and cloud cases, local Python exercises, and reproducible reports. Python 3.10+ for coding.
- [Tenant isolation under pressure](https://kashsec.vercel.app/expert-labs/tenant-boundary.html): Review an invoice API where a valid session, a support role, and a client-supplied tenant create three different trust boundaries.
- [Signed once, processed twice](https://kashsec.vercel.app/expert-labs/webhook-replay.html): Separate message integrity, freshness, and idempotency in a payment webhook. A valid signature is only one of the three checks.
- [The signed artifact from the wrong build](https://kashsec.vercel.app/expert-labs/release-trust.html): Review a release gate that accepts any signed artifact. Bind trust to the expected repository, workflow, source ref, environment, and artifact digest.
- [Cloud permissions with a tenant boundary](https://kashsec.vercel.app/expert-labs/cloud-scope.html): Reduce an over-broad object-store grant and prove the intended action, principal, bucket, and tenant prefix. Separate a small contract test from real IAM evaluation.

42 hands-on exercises that run in the browser — simulated terminals,
deliberately vulnerable apps, packet captures, attack chains. Each lab page
describes what it teaches and how to work through it.

- [Terminal Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/terminal.html): A safe, in-browser Linux terminal with a fake filesystem. Practice ls, cd, cat, grep, find, whoami and more without spinning up a VM.
- [Vulnerable Web App](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/webapp.html): A tiny deliberately-broken app for practicing XSS and login-bypass. Runs entirely in-browser; no server to attack, nothing to install.
- [SQL Injection Sandbox](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/sqli.html): A fake login backed by a simulated database. Watch your input become SQL, then bypass the login with a classic injection.
- [Phishing Spotter](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/phishing.html): Real email or phish? Call each one, then see the exact red flags you spotted (or missed). Trains the instinct that stops most attacks.
- [Packet Capture Viewer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/pcap.html): Load a sample capture and explore protocols, IPs, and payloads — the same "read the traffic" muscle Wireshark builds.
- [IDOR Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/idor.html): A fake "my invoices" page. Change one number in the URL and see whose data you were never supposed to see.
- [JWT Forgery Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/jwt.html): Tamper with a JSON Web Token — strip the signature, flip a claim, and watch a vulnerable "verify" endpoint accept it anyway.
- [Path Traversal Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/traversal.html): A fake "view file" feature that trusts the filename you give it. Climb out of the intended folder with ../ and read files you shouldn't.
- [SSRF Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/ssrf.html): A "fetch this URL for me" feature with no allowlist. Point it at internal-looking addresses and see what it leaks.
- [XXE Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/xxe.html): An XML upload feature that expands external entities. Smuggle a local file read through a "harmless" XML document.
- [Log Analysis / IR Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/loganalysis.html): A messy auth.log dump from a compromised box. Reconstruct the timeline and find the breach — blue-team skills, not exploitation.
- [OSINT Sandbox](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/osint.html): A safe, fake company profile — practise open-source recon technique without touching anything real.
- [BOLA/BFLA Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/bola-bfla.html): A fake employee-directory API. Read a record that isn't yours, then call an admin-only action with no admin role at all.
- [GraphQL Introspection Abuse](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/graphql-introspection.html): A single /graphql endpoint. Use introspection to map the full schema, then query a field the UI never shows you.
- [Mass Assignment Toy](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/mass-assignment.html): A "update my profile" endpoint that binds whatever JSON you send straight to your account. Find the field that shouldn't be writable.
- [Rate-Limit Bypass Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/rate-limit-bypass.html): A login endpoint that blocks you after 3 bad guesses — but trusts a header you control to decide who "you" are.
- [Prompt Injection Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/prompt-injection.html): Chat with a support bot that's told to never reveal its system prompt. Get it to reveal it anyway.
- [Jailbreak Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/jailbreak.html): An assistant refuses to share a secret code directly. Find a roleplay or hypothetical framing that gets it to comply anyway.
- [Indirect Prompt Injection Challenge](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/indirect-injection.html): You control a job posting an AI assistant is about to summarize for someone else. Plant an instruction it'll follow instead.
- [Agentic Risk Scenario](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/agentic-risk.html): An AI agent with email tool-access is about to process an inbox. Spot and quarantine the malicious email before it acts on it.
- [Active Directory Attack Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/ad-attack.html): A guided walkthrough of BloodHound-style graph recon, Kerberoasting a weak service account, and forging a Golden Ticket.
- [CSRF Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/csrf.html): A "bank" transfer endpoint trusts your cookie alone. Watch a malicious page forge a request on your behalf, then see a CSRF token stop it cold.
- [Command Injection Sandbox](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/cmdinjection.html): A "ping this host" tool glues your input into a real shell command. Chain a second command onto the intended one.
- [Open Redirect Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/openredirect.html): A login page trusts a returnUrl parameter completely. Turn a genuinely trusted link into a post-login phishing weapon.
- [Clickjacking Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/clickjacking.html): An invisible iframe sits on top of a fake game button. See exactly how a real click lands on a hidden "delete account" button instead.
- [Insecure Deserialization Toy](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/deserialization.html): A "remember me" cookie is a trusted, deserialized object. Add one field to grant yourself admin with zero login.
- [Subdomain Takeover Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/subdomaintakeover.html): Five DNS records, one dangling CNAME pointing at a deleted third-party resource. Find it before someone else claims it.
- [DNS Recon Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/dnsrecon.html): A simulated dig. Query a target's likely subdomains and build a map of its real, sometimes-forgotten attack surface.
- [Windows Privesc Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/winprivesc.html): A misconfigured service runs as SYSTEM with a writable binary path. Replace it and escalate — no exploit needed.
- [Linux Privesc Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/linuxprivesc.html): Enumerate SUID binaries on a simulated box and find the one GTFOBins turns straight into a root shell.
- [Kerberoasting Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/kerberoast.html): Request a service ticket for a weak-password service account, then crack the offline-crackable hash it hands you.
- [Cloud IAM Misconfig Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/iammisconfig.html): A role holds one deceptively small permission. Chain it into full account takeover through iam:PassRole.
- [Docker Escape Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/dockerescape.html): A container mounts the host's Docker socket. Use it to spin up a privileged container and step onto the host itself.
- [Malware Strings Triage Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/malwarestrings.html): A raw strings dump from a suspicious binary. Spot the IOCs — a C2 domain, a mutex, a registry key — before touching a disassembler.
- [YARA Rule Builder Challenge](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/yarabuilder.html): Three malware samples, one clean file. Write a YARA rule that matches every sample and nothing else.
- [Race Condition Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/racecondition.html): A one-time coupon, redeemed with a check-then-act flaw. Fire requests fast enough and redeem it far more than once.
- [Webhook Signature Forgery Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/webhookforge.html): Forge an HMAC-signed webhook without the secret, then flip on signature verification and watch it get rejected.
- [OAuth Redirect URI Hijack Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/oauthredirect.html): An authorization server validates redirect_uri loosely. Steal an authorization code by redirecting it to your own endpoint.
- [Vendor Risk Tiering Simulator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/vendortiering.html): Six vendors, six very different data-access levels. Tier them correctly and decide who needs a full security review.
- [Incident Response Tabletop](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/irtabletop.html): A branching ransomware scenario. Make the containment and communication calls a real incident commander has to make under pressure.
- [Password Cracking Lab](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/passwordcrack.html): Four hashed passwords, one wordlist. See exactly which ones fall to a dictionary attack and which survive it — and why.
- [Leaked Secret Hunt](https://kashsec.vercel.app/labs/clouddockersecrets.html): A public GitHub repo dump. Find the hardcoded API key an automated scanner would catch in minutes — before an attacker does.

## Security tools

32 working utilities — encoders, analysers, calculators and generators. All
client-side; input never leaves the browser.

- [Encoder / Decoder](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/encoder.html): Base64, URL, and Hex — encode or decode text both ways.
- [Hash Generator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/hash.html): SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 of any text, via the browser's crypto engine.
- [JWT Decoder](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/jwt.html): Decode a JSON Web Token's header and payload and read its claims. No signature verification.
- [CVSS 4.0 + 3.1 Calculator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/cvss.html): Build a CVSS vector and calculate Base, Threat, and Environmental severity locally.
- [Subnet Calculator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/subnet.html): IPv4 CIDR → network, broadcast, host range, mask, and host count.
- [Password Strength](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/password.html): Rough entropy and crack-time estimate for a password, with feedback.
- [Cipher Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/cipher.html): Caesar/ROT, XOR, and Vigenère — the classic ciphers from the CTF zone.
- [Regex Tester](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/regex.html): Test a regular expression against sample text with live match highlighting and capture groups.
- [Hash Identifier](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/hashid.html): Paste a hash and get likely algorithms, guessed from its length and character set.
- [Security Header Analyzer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/headers.html): Paste HTTP response headers and get a graded report on the security headers present and missing.
- [Vulnerability Report Writer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/vulnreport.html): A guided form that forces good structure — title, severity, steps to reproduce, impact, remediation — then exports clean Markdown or a printable PDF.
- [Resume/LinkedIn Keyword Helper](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/resumehelper.html): Paste a job description, see which security keywords you already cover (based on completed paths) and which are gaps.
- [Portfolio Project Generator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/portfoliogen.html): Guided starter briefs for real portfolio projects, with a write-up template you can export.
- [Secure Code Review Toy](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/codereview.html): Paste a code snippet and get flagged patterns — eval, string-built SQL, hardcoded secrets. Not a real SAST tool, but trains the eye.
- [MITRE ATT&CK Mapper](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/attckmap.html): A searchable reference of real ATT&CK tactics and techniques, tied back to where this course covers each one.
- [STRIDE Threat-Model Worksheet](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/stride.html): A guided Spoofing/Tampering/Repudiation/Info-Disclosure/DoS/Elevation worksheet, exportable as Markdown.
- [CIDR Overlap Checker](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/cidroverlap.html): Check whether two CIDR ranges overlap — catches conflicting firewall/routing rules before they cause an outage.
- [User-Agent String Parser](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/useragent.html): Break down a User-Agent string into OS, browser, and version — and flag common automated-client patterns.
- [Entropy Calculator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/entropy.html): Shannon entropy of any text — a genuine static-analysis signal for spotting packed or encrypted data.
- [Raw HTTP Request Builder](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/httpbuilder.html): Build a raw HTTP request from method, path, headers, and body — see exactly what goes over the wire.
- [Log Grep / Filter Playground](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/logparser.html): Filter a block of log lines with a regex — the exact "find the signal in the noise" skill IR work depends on.
- [Risk Register Builder](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/riskregister.html): Add risks with likelihood and impact, get an auto-scored severity, and export the register as Markdown.
- [Dependency / SBOM Risk Checker](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/sbomcheck.html): Paste a dependency list and flag ones matching a known-vulnerable version range.
- [Email Header Analyzer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/emailheaders.html): Paste raw email headers and get flagged for From/Return-Path mismatches, SPF failures, and missing DKIM.
- [Password Policy Checker](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/passpolicy.html): Test a password against a configurable length/complexity policy, rule by rule.
- [VLSM Subnet Planner](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/vlsm.html): Plan variable-length subnets across several different host-count requirements from one base network.
- [Simplified YARA Rule Tester](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/yaratester.html): Test a small set of required strings against sample content and see whether your rule matches.
- [Incident Severity & SLA Calculator](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/slacalc.html): Impact × urgency in, a priority tier and realistic remediation SLA out.
- [Compliance Control Mapper](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/controlmapper.html): Look up how one control area maps across SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and PCI-DSS.
- [Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange Visualizer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/dhvisualizer.html): Watch two sides land on the same shared secret without ever transmitting it, with small real numbers.
- [Base32 / Base85 Encoder](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/base32.html): Encode or decode text in Base32 or Base85 — the less common encodings you'll still run into in CTFs.
- [Timing Attack Visualizer](https://kashsec.vercel.app/tools/timingviz.html): See exactly why a naive string comparison leaks how many leading characters were correct — and why constant-time comparison fixes it.

## Practice and assessment

- [Practice tasks](https://kashsec.vercel.app/practice.html): 104 typed-answer tasks across every path — compute a subnet, write a find command, read a phishing URL. Answers are hashed and explanations encrypted, so the questions are listed but the answers are not.
- [Timed mock exams](https://kashsec.vercel.app/exam.html): Three papers (90/40/20 questions) under a clock, scored with a per-path breakdown.
